title: ClickHouse: diamonds CSV arrives as columns, not text blobs
summary: Loads the 53,940-row diamonds CSV into ClickHouse and checks whether each CSV row became a table row with its own columns (carat, price, ...). Known defect: today the file is stored as a few hundred text chunks, so this scenario is expected to fail.

steps.title: Drop the ClickHouse table diamonds
steps.explain: Starts from a clean slate so everything found later was written by this run.

steps.title: Count the data rows in the source CSV
steps.explain: The number of rows a correct load must produce.

steps.title: List the table columns (Before)
steps.explain: Before the run the table does not exist, so it has no columns.

args.sql: SELECT name, type FROM system.columns WHERE database = 'openetl' AND table = 'diamonds' ORDER BY position

steps.title: Run the ch_diamonds pipeline
steps.explain: Runs the real pipeline. Everything below checks what it produced.

steps.title: Job finished with status COMPLETED
steps.explain: The job itself reports success; the checks below test whether that is true.

steps.title: Job reported no warnings
steps.explain: Any warning would hint at skipped data.

steps.title: List the table columns (After)
steps.explain: Shows what the table looks like after the run.

args.sql: SELECT name, type FROM system.columns WHERE database = 'openetl' AND table = 'diamonds' ORDER BY position

steps.title: Count rows in the diamonds table
steps.explain: The real number of rows ClickHouse holds.

steps.title: Row count equals the source CSV rows
steps.explain: A correct load stores one row per CSV row.

steps.title: Count columns named carat
steps.explain: A correct load has a column for each CSV header.

args.sql: SELECT count() FROM system.columns WHERE database = 'openetl' AND table = 'diamonds' AND name = 'carat'

steps.title: The table has a carat column
steps.explain: Without it the diamond data cannot be queried by carat or price.

steps.title: Count columns named price
steps.explain: The price column is the second check that the CSV was split into fields.

args.sql: SELECT count() FROM system.columns WHERE database = 'openetl' AND table = 'diamonds' AND name = 'price'

steps.title: The table has a price column
